newsitem.title: zaire: LACK OF FUEL DELAYS KABILA TEAM'S TRIP TO KINSHASA.
newsitem.headline: LACK OF FUEL DELAYS KABILA TEAM'S TRIP TO KINSHASA.

text.p: Triumphant Laurent Kabila will send a delegation to the Zairean capital Kinshasa on Sunday to reassure the people about security, a senior Alliance official said on Sunday. But departure was delayed by a shortage of aviation fuel.

Meantime in Lubumbashi, South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki was expected later on Sunday to be the first foreign dignitary to meet Kabila since the rebels proclaimed victory in the civil war, Alliance officials told Reuters.

The delegation was due to leave Lubumbashi within hours. It would be headed by Deogratius Bugera, Secretary-General of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo, and would include "information minister" Raphael Ghenda.
"When we take a town, we always send a team. They have to reassure the population and explain our message," said Mwawapanga Mwana Nanga, the rebel finance minister.
Asked when Kabila would go to the capital, he said: "In the next couple of days or a few days. It is at his discretion."
Aviation sources said the delegation's departure was delayed by a lack of jet fuel but it still planned to leave.

Delegation member Letya Mussa Nyembo said it was not part of the mission's mandate to start negotiations with Kinshasa's politicians on a government but merely to "see how to run Kinshasa administratively, how to occupy the city and run it".
Letya said resistance in Kinshasa was so far negligible.

Kabila, 56, declared himself head of state in a statement he read at his headquarters in the southern mining city of Lubumbashi on Saturday as his forces moved into the capital Kinshasa virtually unopposed, to the cheers of residents.

The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) on Sunday acknowledged the civil war triumph of Kabila and his rebels and called for a broad-based transitional authority representing Zaireans of other political shades.
"Mr Kabila and the AFDL (rebel alliance) have won the civil war and the challenge before them now is to win and consolidate the peace," said OAU Secretary-General Salim Ahmed Salim.
"I hope that when Mr Kabila forms his government of transition, it will be a broad-based one, incorporating other elements of the Congo-Zaire society," Salim said in a statement.
